approved: Migration Legislation Amendment (Cessation of Visa Labels) Bill 2015
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would remove laws about visa labels that are no longer used.
It would repeal the Migration (Visa Evidence) Charge Act 2012 and delete related sections of the Migration Act 1958.
The changes would take effect the day after the bill becomes law.
Repeals the Migration (Visa Evidence) Charge Act 2012.
Removes definitions and provisions about visa evidence from the Migration Act 1958.
Makes technical amendments to remove references to repealed parts of the Migration Act.
The Department of Immigration and Border Protection and clients who previously requested visa labels.

The speaker supported the Migration Legislation Amendment (Cessation of Visa Labels) Bill 2015, which gives statutory effect to ending visa labels; monthly issuances dropped from about 100,000 in 2011 to 2,816 in August 2015, and industry stakeholders were consulted and supportive.
